TRANSCRIPTION by eye from page images (no text layer); whitespace collapsed, form chrome dropped, typos kept. public_note: Response options are listed without their 0-3 scores because the authors did not publish which option earns which score, so the option text cannot be joined to resp; the English text is IRW's own translation of the Indonesian form.

note: CODE DERIVATION: pattern 4 (script-generated integer) -- data/deception_professors.R drops 20 covariate/reviewer columns and 18 open-response indicator columns, builds reason_less_rigorous and reason_no_deception by case_when over those indicators, pivots, and assigns item=row_number() over unique(item). Re-ran the script (labelled::remove_labels swapped for haven::zap_labels) over the OSF .sav: 1 decept_percent_psych, 2 decept_percent_eco, 3 decept_percent_socsci, 4 decept_rigorous, 5 orthogonal_to_rigor, 6 psych_considerdecept, 7 eco_considerdecept, 8 gensci_considerdecept, 9 eco_poolbans, 10 eco_journalbans, 11 psych_poolbans, 12 psych_journalban, 13 gensci_journalban, 14 banharmful_eco, 15 banharmful_psych, 16 banharmful_gensci, 17 you_percent_decept, 18 you_worry_rigor, 19 you_limit_decept, 20 reason_less_rigorous, 21 reason_no_deception. Re-run reproduces the live table exactly: 11928 rows, per-item n and full resp frequency tables equal for 21/21 items, all 21 distributions mutually distinct (verify_deception_professors.R). WORDS: item_text is the .sav variable label verbatim (codebook identical) except: items 1-3 replace the label's internal suffix ' - PSYCH/ - ECO/ - SOCSCI' with the ESM Appendix 1 row labels 'Psychology/Economics/Social Science in general'; items 14-16 replace '...  for ECO/PSYCH/GENSCI' with the ESM's '... for economics?/psychology?/science in general?' (ESM ellipsis character rendered as '...', doubled space removed); items 20 and 21 carry the shared label prefix common to their component indicator variables ('... Please elaborate - Open Response Coding' / "Why don't you use deception in your experimental designs?- Open Response Coding"), since these two items are IRW constructs with no single source label. instructions is the ESM Appendix 1 introduction verbatim (title 'Perceptions of Deception in Social Science Research' also from there). OPTIONS: from .sav value labels verbatim. Items 4 and 18: .sav 1=Yes 2=No, processing script recodes 2->0, so resp 1=Yes, 0=No. Items 9-16: .sav labels 1, 4 ('Midpoint') and 7; the 4='Midpoint' label was DROPPED because ESM Appendix 1 shows the administered scale as '1- ..., 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 - ...' with only endpoints labelled; points 2-6 left blank. Items 5, 20, 21: option_text is the parenthetical of each coding variable's label verbatim, including source typos ('decption', 'wont', 'misinterpretted', 'relevent') -- these are coder categories for free-text answers, not options respondents saw; item 20/21 codes follow the script's case_when order. Items 1-3 and 17 are 0-100 sliders: one row per observed resp value, option_text blank. Item 13 (gensci_journalban, 'Should deceptive practices be banned in general science journals?') is in the .sav and codebook but absent from ESM Appendix 1, which lists only (9) pools and (10) psychology journals; label shipped as-is. RIGHTS: ad hoc survey written by the study authors; no restriction on the questionnaire located (OSF node CC BY 4.0; article/ESM carry only a bare '(c) 2019 The Psychonomic Society' notice, which is not a term governing the instrument per SKILL rights section). Nothing to block.
public_note: Item 5 (coded 'not relevant to rigor') holds only the value 1 -- respondents not given that code are missing, not 0; items 20 and 21 each keep only the first-listed code for respondents whose free-text answer received several (23 of 267 and 46 of 306); and item 17 (percentage of own designs using deception) records 0 for the 357 respondents who were never asked it because they do not use deception.
